pairs.evidence: src/types/prompt-evolution.ts:107 The prompt A/B rail sums duration over every trial, including failed runs and runs booked at 0 ms, then uses that mean to crown a winner on near-ties, so the tie-break compares a mix of outcomes and unmeasured runs rather than the cost of successful work.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/prompt-evolution/verdict.ts:158 The mean includes failed trials and has no both-succeeded view or incomplete state; the recipe path books trials with no duration, which default to 0 ms and enter the mean as instantaneous.
src/lib/prompt-evolution/verdict.ts:156 Duration acts as a second objective inside the verdict instead of a declared threshold, and no constraint can block a winner.

src/lib/prompt-evolution/judge-fitness.ts:136 Pass counts pool llm-panel, vlm and human judges and ignore rubricVersion and contentHash, so mixed instruments form one rate and a verdict on earlier content can be charged to the variant now stamped on the artifact.

src/lib/prompt-evolution/ab-testing.ts:213 Decide-now crowns a winner at 3 serves per arm with no z check, by duration on a tie; auto-conclude records null below the weakest band, but this path turns a measured tie into a winner with a caution attached.

src/app/api/checklist/complete/route.ts:79 A trial's success comes from the run's own callback and a missing field counts as success; auto-conclude can crown a winner on this self-reported basis when judged evidence is short.
src/stores/promptEvolutionStore.ts:115 Each trial is one success bit, and arms carry only rates and counts, so two arms at the same rate cannot be told apart by how their runs failed.
src/lib/prompt-evolution/verdict.ts:122 Epsilon-greedy serving gives arms unequal N, and the verdict note states both arms' counts in the same sentence as the result.
src/types/prompt-evolution.ts:157 The treatment is prompt text applied at dispatch, not a capability the candidate may decline.
